info.title: API Dropshipper
info.description:
Dropshipper-facing public REST API. Place and confirm orders, browse the catalog, read your shops and track shipment incidences — the same surface the Dropea front-end uses, exposed for your own integrations. Public REST API for Dropea. All endpoints require an API Key Bearer token and are subject to per-key rate limits and permission checks. --- ## Getting started First, **select your market** in the **Server** dropdown (top of the page) — Dropea has one deployment per market (PT / ES / IT / MX / CL) and each has its own host. The snippets below use the **PT** host (the default); if you operate in another market, swap `pt.` for `es.` / `it.` / `mx.` / `cl.`. The snippets below walk a full order from zero. Replace `` with your key and run them top to bottom. **1. Create an API Key** — from the **API Keys** section of your Dropea dashboard. Copy the token (shown once) into the requests below. **2. Confirm who you are** ```bash curl https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/me \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` **3. List your shops** — you need a `store_id` to place an order. It is the `id` field of each shop here. ```bash curl https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/shops \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` **4. Browse products** — each product carries a `variants` array; each variant's `variant_id` is the value you put into the order line items. ```bash curl "https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/products?page=1&limit=20" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` **5. Create the order** — send a unique `Idempotency-Key` so a network retry never double-creates. ```bash curl -X POST https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/orders \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: 1f1c9e2a-7b3e-4f0a-9c2d-9d6f0a8e1b22" \ -d '{ "store_id": 1024, "payment_method": "COD", "line_items": [ { "variant_id": 5567, "quantity": 2, "unit_price": 19.99 } ], "customer_details": { "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com", "phone": "+34600123456", "shipping_address": { "first_name": "Ada", "last_name": "Lovelace", "address_line_1": "Calle Mayor 1", "city": "Madrid", "state": "Madrid", "postal_code": "28013", "country": "ES" } } }' ``` Order creation is **synchronous with a 15-second budget** (see *Creating an order* below). On success you get **200** with the full order. If the underlying saga has not settled in time you get **504** with an `operation_id` to poll. **6. Confirm the order** — placement leaves the order in `PENDING`; confirm it to hand it to the supplier. ```bash curl -X POST https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/orders/1001/confirm \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: 7a2b9c3d-4e5f-4a1b-8c2d-3e6f9a0b1c4d" ``` **7. Stay in sync** — subscribe webhooks (recommended; see the **Webhooks** section) to receive `order.created`, `order.status.changed` and `order.cancelled` pushes, or poll the order / operation endpoints. --- ## Request fields Fields whose source is not obvious when building an order request: - **`store_id`** — Sequential shop number. Take it from the `id` field of `GET /dropshipper/shops`. - **`line_items[]`** — array of order line items (one or more). Each item carries `variant_id`, `quantity` and `unit_price`: - **`variant_id`** — sequential variant number. Take it from `products[].variants[].variant_id` of `GET /dropshipper/products`. - **`unit_price`** — price per unit charged to the end customer. See *Pricing rules* below — it is validated, not free-form. - **`carrier`** — Optional carrier code. Valid codes come from `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`. Omit to let the platform resolve the carrier for the destination country. A carrier that does not operate in the destination country is rejected with `CARRIER_COUNTRY_NOT_COVERED`. - **`service_type`** — Optional. Valid codes are in `services[].code` of the carrier in `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`. - **`payment_method`** — One of `COD`, `PAYPAL`, `STRIPE`, `SHOPIFY_PAYMENTS`, `PAID`, `MANUAL`, `OTHER`. Any value of the enum is accepted — there is **no per-market gating**. `COD` and `MANUAL` are treated as cash-on-delivery for commission purposes. - **Phone fields** — `phone` (the full number, e.g. `+34600123456`) is the only required phone field. Optionally you may also send it split into `phone_country` (ISO-2 country, e.g. `ES`), `area_code` (dialing prefix, e.g. `+34`) and `phone_number` (the local subscriber number) — these three are optional. ### Pricing rules `unit_price` is **the price you charge the end customer**, and you set it per line item. It is **not** free-form, but the floor is checked **per order, not per line**: an unpaid order (`payment_method` `COD` or `MANUAL`) is rejected with **422 `ORDER_TOTAL_BELOW_COST`** when the order total is below the combined wholesale cost of everything it carries, i.e. below `Σ(wholesale_price × quantity)`. This means an individual line **may** be priced below its own wholesale price — even at `0`, which is how a gifted item such as a shipping box is sent — as long as the rest of the order covers it. What you may never do is collect less than the total cost of the goods. Two cases skip the check entirely: orders already paid by the buyer (any `payment_method` other than `COD` / `MANUAL`) and orders whose total is `0`. For a pack (bundle variant) the cost is derived from the wholesale prices of its sub order line items scaled by the units each one contributes to the pack, using the composition of **this order** — the catalog one, or the one you set with `PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}` (see "Editing a pack" there). Changing a pack's sub order line items changes that cost; `unit_price` does not change by itself. --- ## Creating an order Order creation runs a distributed saga (stock reservation, pricing, fulfilment routing). The endpoint blocks for up to **15 seconds**: - **Settled in time → 200** with the full created order in `data`. - **Not settled in 15s → 504** with `{ "data": { "operation_id": "...", "status": "pending" } }`. The `operation_id` is **the same value as** your `Idempotency-Key`, so poll with the key you already sent: ```bash curl https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/operations/ \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` The operation `status` is one of `in_progress`, `completed` or `failed`. On `completed` the order is created; on `failed` the order was not created and `failure` explains why. --- ## Order lifecycle An order moves through a status machine. The principal statuses are `DRAFT → PENDING → CONFIRMED → PROCESSING → SHIPPING → FINISH` (plus `ERROR` for anomalies). Each step has a sub-status (e.g. `PROCESSING.PICKING`, `SHIPPING.SHIPPED`, `FINISH.DELIVERED`). | Status | Triggered by | Webhook | |--------|--------------|---------| | `PENDING` | Dropshipper creates the order (`POST /dropshipper/orders`) | `order.created` | | `CONFIRMED` | Dropshipper confirms (`POST /dropshipper/orders/{id}/confirm`) | `order.status.changed` | | `PROCESSING` (`PICKING`) | Supplier starts preparing (`POST /supplier/orders/state/preparing`) | `order.status.changed` | | `PROCESSING` (`PACKED`) | Supplier finishes packing (`POST /supplier/orders/state/prepared`) | `order.status.changed` | | `SHIPPING` | Carrier picks up / transits the shipment | `order.status.changed` | | `FINISH` (`DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, ...) | Carrier delivery or cancellation | `order.status.changed` / `order.cancelled` | Happy-path sequence (dropshipper → supplier → delivery): ```text PENDING order created by the dropshipper | v CONFIRMED dropshipper confirms | v PROCESSING.PICKING supplier starts preparing | v PROCESSING.PACKED supplier finishes packing (carrier hand-off) | v SHIPPING carrier picks up / in transit | v FINISH.DELIVERED delivered (or FINISH.CANCELLED on cancellation) ``` Because the envelope carries no `previous_state`, detect transitions by caching the last `status` / `sub_status` per order and diffing on each `order.status.changed` delivery. ## Authentication Every request must carry your API Key as a Bearer token: ```bash Authorization: Bearer ``` Create the key from the **API Keys** section of your Dropea dashboard. The token is shown **once** at creation — store it securely; it cannot be retrieved again. Keys are validated **offline** (the token is self-contained), so there is no token-introspection round-trip on the hot path. > ⚠️ **Shared devices:** for convenience, the **Authorize** button in this > documentation keeps the key you enter in your browser (localStorage). Do > **not** paste a real API Key on a shared or public computer — use a private > window, or clear the authorization when you finish. --- ## Server — pick your market Dropea runs **one deployment per market**, each with its own host. **Select the market you operate in** from the **Server** dropdown at the top of this page — every "Test request" then targets that host. The available hosts are: | Market | Base URL | |--------|----------| | Portugal (PT) — default | `https://pt.public-api.dropea.com` | | Spain (ES) | `https://es.public-api.dropea.com` | | Italy (IT) | `https://it.public-api.dropea.com` | | Mexico (MX) | `https://mx.public-api.dropea.com` | | Chile (CL) | `https://cl.public-api.dropea.com` | The API surface and this documentation are **identical across markets** — only the host changes. The `curl` examples below use the **PT** host (the default); if you operate in another market, swap `pt.` for `es.` / `it.` / `mx.` / `cl.`. --- ## Rate limiting You can make up to **60 requests per minute** (the limit depends on your role). The window is **rolling**, not fixed: at any moment the API counts the requests from the **last 60 seconds** — it does NOT reset on the clock minute. As your older requests age past 60 seconds, that capacity frees up again. Every response tells you where you stand: - **`X-RateLimit-Limit`** — your maximum requests per window (60). - **`X-RateLimit-Remaining`** — how many you have left right now. - **`X-RateLimit-Window`** — the window length in seconds (60). If you go over, the API returns **429 Too Many Requests** with a **`Retry-After: 60`** header — wait that many seconds, then retry. --- ## Idempotency Mutating requests (`POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, and selected `DELETE` endpoints) **require** an `Idempotency-Key` header so retries never duplicate side effects. Send a unique key per logical operation — a **UUID v4** is recommended; the format must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,255}`. ```bash Idempotency-Key: 1f1c9e2a-7b3e-4f0a-9c2d-9d6f0a8e1b22 ``` Semantics (keys are retained for **24h**, backed by Redis): | Situation | Result | |-----------|--------| | First request with a key | Processed normally; the response is cached under the key. | | Replay with the **same key + same body** | The cached response is returned with header `Idempotent-Replay: true`. | | Same key, **different body** | **422** — a key may not be reused for a different payload. | | Same key while the first call is **still in flight** | **409** — the original operation has not settled yet. | | Original returned **5xx** | Not cached — you may safely retry with the same key. | `GET` requests are inherently idempotent and ignore the header. --- ## Error format Every error shares the same envelope: ```json { "success": false, "message": "human readable summary", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "ValidationFailure", "message": "detailed cause", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 400 } } ``` `failure.type` maps to the HTTP status: - `ValidationFailure` → **400** - `UnauthorizedFailure` → **401** - `ForbiddenFailure` → **403** - `NotFoundFailure` → **404** - `ConflictFailure` → **409** - `BusinessFailure` → **422** - (rate limit) → **429** - `ServerFailure` / `DatabaseFailure` → **500** - `NetworkFailure` → **503** - (saga timeout) → **504** Representative examples:
401 — missing or invalid API Key ```json { "success": false, "message": "invalid or missing API key", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "UnauthorizedFailure", "message": "API key is invalid or expired", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 401 } } ```
403 — key lacks the required permission ```json { "success": false, "message": "permission denied", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "ForbiddenFailure", "message": "API key is not allowed to perform this action", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 403 } } ```
404 — resource not found ```json { "success": false, "message": "resource not found", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "NotFoundFailure", "message": "order not found", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 404 } } ```
422 — business rule rejected the request ```json { "success": false, "message": "order total below wholesale cost", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "BusinessFailure", "message": "Order total 5 is below the wholesale cost 8 of its items", "code": "ORDER_TOTAL_BELOW_COST", "httpStatusCode": 422 } } ```
429 — rate limit exceeded ```json { "success": false, "message": "rate limit exceeded", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "RateLimitFailure", "message": "too many requests, retry after 60s", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 429 } } ```

bearerAuth.description:
Long-lived API Key issued by Dropea, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

**How to get one:** sign in to your Dropea dashboard → **Settings → API Keys** → **Create API Key**, pick the scopes you need, and copy the token shown **once** at creation time. If you lose it, regenerate — Dropea does not store the plaintext.

This is **not** your dashboard session token: do not paste anything you see in your browser DevTools. Treat the API Key like a password and keep it server-side.

The required permissions per operation are listed in each endpoint under the `x-dropea-permissions` extension.

IdempotencyKeyHeader.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyHeader.description: Unique key per request (UUID v4 recommended). Generate a fresh value on every call — replaying the same key within 24h returns the cached response with `Idempotent-Replay: true`, which is intended for retry/network failure scenarios, not for normal back-to-back requests.

IdempotencyKeyHeaderOptional.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyHeaderOptional.description: Unique key per request (UUID v4 recommended). Optional on this endpoint — if omitted, the server generates one and echoes it back as the `Idempotency-Key` response header, usable to poll `GET /operations/:operation_id`. If sent, replaying the same key within 24h returns the cached response with `Idempotent-Replay: true`.

Failure.description: Error envelope returned by the API on any non-2xx response.

code.description: Machine-readable business error code, when available (e.g. business rule violations). `null` for generic failures.

BasicFailureResponse.description: Standard failure envelope used by every endpoint.

PaginationMeta.description: Pagination metadata describing the current page of results.

total.description: Total number of items across all pages.

limit.description: Page size requested by the caller (capped server-side).

total_pages.description: Total number of pages given the current `limit`.

Pagination.description:
Standard envelope returned by every paginated list endpoint.
The page items live in `items` and pagination metadata in `pagination`.
Endpoint-specific shapes extend this via `allOf` and override the
`items` array element type (e.g. `Order`, `Product`, `Shop`).

OrderLineItem.description: A single line item inside an Order (response shape). Product/variant names and SKU are resolved server-side at creation time and are read-only for consumers.

ean.description: EAN/UPC code. Leading zeros are NOT preserved.

variant_type.description:
- `SIMPLE` — standard product variant (most common value on reads).
- `DEFAULT` — a standard single variant (synonym of `SIMPLE`).
- `BUNDLE` — a pack: one line that ships several products together.

How a pack is shown depends on the surface:

- **Dropshipper** (`/dropshipper/orders`): the pack stays ONE line
  with `variant_type: BUNDLE`, and its content is listed in
  `sub_order_line_items` (which products, and how many units of
  each per pack). You can change that content with
  `PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}` — see "Editing a pack" there.
- **Supplier** (`/supplier/orders`): the pack is replaced by one
  row per component. On such a row this is the type the catalog
  reports for that component, and is never `BUNDLE` — a component
  is not itself a pack. It is absent when the row was built from
  the frozen composition instead of the catalog (see the fallback
  note on the supplier endpoints): the snapshot freezes identity,
  not type.

sub_order_line_items.description:
The content of a pack line: one entry per product the pack
contains, with the units of that product in ONE pack.

- Present only when `variant_type` is `BUNDLE`, and only on the
  dropshipper surface (the supplier surface lists the pack's
  products as separate rows instead).
- It reflects the composition **frozen on this order**: the
  catalog composition at the time of sale, or the one you set
  later with `PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}`. Editing the pack in
  the catalog does not change orders already placed.
- It may be **missing on old orders** that were placed before
  Dropea froze the composition on the order. It is then omitted as
  a whole — never listed partially.

Units actually shipped of a sub line = line `quantity` × sub
line `quantity`.

source_bundle_id.description:
Variant number of the pack this row came from. Present ONLY on the
supplier surface (`GET /supplier/orders`, `GET /supplier/orders/{order_number}`),
on rows produced by expanding a pack into its components — see the
note on that endpoint. Absent on every regular line item and on the
whole dropshipper surface, where a pack stays one line and lists
its content in `sub_order_line_items`.

external_name.description:
Original line item name as it appeared in the source channel. For
Shopify-sourced orders this is the Shopify line_item title; `null`
for orders created through other channels.

SubOrderLineItem.description:
One product inside a pack line (a line with `variant_type: BUNDLE`),
with how many units of it ONE pack contains.

- **Read** (`OrderLineItem.sub_order_line_items`): the product the
  pack ships, identified by its public numbers, plus its frozen names
  and SKU.
- **Write** (`OrderLineItemInput.sub_order_line_items`, only on
  `PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}`): send only `variant_id` and
  `quantity`. The read-only fields are resolved by the server and are
  rejected if sent.

Units actually shipped of a sub line = line `quantity` × sub line
`quantity`. Example: a line with `quantity: 3` (three packs) whose
sub line has `quantity: 2` ships 6 units of that product.

variant_id.description: Human-readable sequential variant number of the product inside the pack. Same numbering as `OrderLineItem.variant_id` and as `variant_id` in the product catalog. Must not be repeated inside the same pack.

quantity.description: Units of this product per pack unit (NOT the total). Total units shipped = line `quantity` × this value.

product_id.description: Human-readable sequential product number of the product inside the pack. Always present on reads.

product_name.description: Product name, frozen on the order. Omitted when the order did not freeze it.

variant_name.description: Variant name, frozen on the order. Omitted when the order did not freeze it.

sku.description: SKU of the variant, frozen on the order. Omitted when the variant has no SKU.

OrderLineItemInput.description:
Line item accepted by `POST /dropshipper/orders` and, extended with
`sub_order_line_items`, by `PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}`.
`variant_id` is the human-readable sequential variant number. Product
names and SKU are derived by the server from `variant_id` — they cannot
be set by the caller.

variant_id.description: Human-readable sequential variant number. For a pack line, the pack's own variant number (the line whose `variant_type` is `BUNDLE`).

quantity.description: Units of this line. For a pack line, the number of packs.

unit_price.description: Price per unit charged to the end customer. For a pack line, the price of one pack. It is never recalculated from the sub order line items.

address_line_1.description: First address line. The carrier receives BOTH lines joined by `, `, and that joined string must not exceed 200 characters when the destination country is MX and 100 characters for every other country (`ADDRESS_LENGTH_EXCEEDED`) — so the real limit is shared between the two lines and includes the 2-character separator. Outside MX, two lines of 60 and 40 characters are rejected (102), while 50 and 48 are accepted (exactly 100).

address_line_2.description: Optional second address line. Counts towards the same limit as `address_line_1` (200 characters with destination MX, 100 elsewhere); when left empty no separator is added.

postal_code.description: Postal code of the address. Required in most markets. In a market whose carriers do not work by postal code (Chile), the postal code is inferred from `state` (the province) and overwrites the one sent, so it may be omitted there; a province that cannot be mapped is rejected with `PROVINCE_NOT_COVERED`. Elsewhere a missing postal code is rejected with `MISSING_POSTAL_CODE`.

field_extra_1.description: MX: colonia (neighbourhood), up to 60 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

field_extra_2.description: MX: entre calles (cross streets), up to 100 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

field_extra_3.description: MX: referencias (delivery references), up to 150 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

OrderShippingAddress.description:
Shipping address as returned on every order read (create / get / list).
The customer contact fields (`full_name`, `email`, `phone_number`) are
merged into this object on output — there is no separate
`customer_details` on read. Phone is exposed combined (`phone_number`)
and, when available, split into `phone_country` / `area_code` /
`phone_without_prefix` (all `null` when the order was created with a
single combined `phone`).

field_extra_1.description: MX: colonia (neighbourhood), up to 60 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

field_extra_2.description: MX: entre calles (cross streets), up to 100 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

field_extra_3.description: MX: referencias (delivery references), up to 150 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

validation_result_summary.description:
Outcome of the address check performed by the sales channel when
the order was imported (Shopify). Use it to spot addresses that
may need review before shipping. `null` or absent when the channel
performed no check — notably for orders not created through it.

The value is passed through from Shopify verbatim
(`MailingAddressValidationResult`):

- `NO_ISSUES` — validated, no problems found.
- `WARNING` — validated, may contain invalid information.
- `ERROR` — validated, very likely to contain invalid information.

Treat the list as open: since the value is relayed unchanged,
a value Shopify adds later reaches you before this documentation
catches up. Do not reject an unknown one.

coordinates_validated.description: Whether the address coordinates were validated at import time.

CustomerDetails.description:
Customer + shipping data accepted when **creating or updating** an order
(request shape). On read the order does NOT echo a nested
`customer_details`; this data is flattened into `shipping_address`
(see `OrderShippingAddress`).

Order.description: Order entity as exposed to external API consumers.

status.description: Top-level lifecycle status. The full mapping (with sub-statuses and descriptions) is exposed by `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/order-statuses`. NOTE: `DELIVERED` top-level is **legacy** — the canonical terminal state is `FINISH` (with `sub_status: DELIVERED`). It is kept in the enum only for historical orders; new orders never reach top-level `DELIVERED`.

sub_status.description: Refines the main `status` with the current step inside it (e.g. `PICKING` while in `PROCESSING`, `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` while in `SHIPPING`). Required to perform state transitions like `Transition orders to prepared`. The `(status, sub_status)` mapping is documented in `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/order-statuses`.

store_owner_id.description: Human-readable sequential user number of the store owner.

total_amount.description: Total the end customer pays for the order. Unrelated to what a supplier is paid — see `total_amount_supplier`.

external_created_at.description: Date the order was created in the origin store (Shopify and future integrations), as opposed to `created_at`, which is when it entered Dropea. The two differ whenever an order failed to sync and was reprocessed later. Absent on orders created manually and on orders predating this field; it is never defaulted to `created_at`.

confirmed_at.description: Timestamp when the dropshipper confirmed the order. Absent until the order leaves PENDING.

processing_at.description: Timestamp when the order entered preparation (PROCESSING). Absent until the order leaves CONFIRMED.

delivered_at.description: Delivery timestamp. Absent until the order is marked as delivered.

rejected_at.description: Timestamp when the order was rejected by the recipient/carrier. Absent until the order is rejected.

fulfillment_type.description: Who fulfills the order — `SUPPLIER` when the supplier ships it directly, `DROPEA` when it ships from a Dropea-managed warehouse (FBD).

carrier.description: Shipping carrier code (e.g. CTT, GLS, TIPSA).

service_type.description: Carrier-specific service code (e.g. `EMS` for CTT, `24` for TIPSA, `74` for GLS).

external_order_id.description:
External order id supplied by the integrator at creation time
(typically the order id from a connected storefront like Shopify,
WooCommerce, Tienda Nube, etc.). Stored as-is and echoed back on
every order read so integrators can correlate Dropea orders with
their external system.

pack_ids.description: Product numbers of any BUNDLE line items on the order. Absent when the order contains no bundles.

notes.description:
Order notes, exposing only the public-safe fields. The internal
author fields (`user_id`, `user_role`, `user_full_name`,
`user_email`) are never included. Absent when the order has no notes.

type.description: Note category as emitted by order-service (e.g. internal vs customer-facing).

tax_data_dropshipper.description:
Dropshipper fiscal identity snapshot, supplier-facing (needed by
the supplier to invoice the dropshipper). Absent when the upstream
order carries no tax data.

has_equivalence_surcharge.description: Whether the dropshipper is under the Spanish equivalence surcharge regime (recargo de equivalencia).

expenses_breakdown.description:
What this order costs you, **scoped to your role** — the same
figures the Dropea dashboard shows you for this order.

Which fields you receive depends on who you are, because the two
sides of an order see different economics: a dropshipper sees what
it is charged, a supplier sees what it is paid. A field you are not
entitled to is **omitted**, never returned as `0` — with one
deliberate exception, the shipping fields on the supplier side,
which are an explicit `0` because shipping is genuinely not billed
to you (see their descriptions).

Absent entirely when the order has not been costed yet.

product_price.description: Cost of the goods. Visible to every role.

fulfillment_extra_unit_price.description: Per-unit fulfillment surcharge beyond the first unit. Visible to every role.

tax_rate_supplier.description: VAT rate applied to the supplier side. Visible to every role.

weight_kg.description: Billable weight used to price shipping and fulfillment, in kg. Visible to every role.

is_estimate.description:
`true` while the figures are a projection, `false` once they are
the definitive costs. Note this flips when the order is costed,
which happens at creation — it does **not** mean the order has
been charged. Use `total_expenses` for that. Visible to every role.

calculated_at.description: When these costs were last computed. Visible to every role.

fulfillment_refused_price.description:
Return-leg fulfillment on a refused order. For a dropshipper,
what you are charged; for a supplier, what you are paid.

shipping_outbound_price.description:
Outbound shipping charged to the dropshipper. `0` for a
supplier, except on a warranty order whose shipping the
supplier pays: then it is the amount charged to the supplier.

shipping_refused_price.description:
Return shipping on a refused order, charged to the dropshipper.
Always `0` for a supplier.

pickup_price.description:
Warranty pickup charged to you: the carrier collects the
defective or wrong item from the customer, a shipment separate
from the replacement (`shipping_outbound_price`). `0` on a
standard order, on a warranty order without pickup, or when the
other party pays it. Its VAT is included in `total_expenses`.

tax_rate_dropea.description: VAT rate applied to the Dropea side. **Dropshipper only.**

equivalence_surcharge_rate.description:
Equivalence-surcharge rate (recargo de equivalencia), when it
applies. Reported at full precision, not rounded to cents.
**Dropshipper only.**

total_expenses.description:
What the order actually cost you — the figure that reconciles
with the charge on your wallet.

Present only once the order reaches a terminal state
(delivered, refused, or lost) and its costs are definitive.
Absent otherwise: before that there is no charge to reconcile
against, and reporting a projection here would read as a
settled fact.

It includes Dropea's own commissions, which are not itemised in
this object, so it is **larger than the sum of the fields you
can see**. That is deliberate: a total that matches what you
were charged is more useful than one you can re-add yourself.

On a **warranty order** it is the sum of what was debited to
you for that order: shipping, pickup, fulfillment and their
VAT, only the legs you pay (each leg has its own payer).

For a **supplier** it is published only on a settled warranty
order where you pay at least one leg; absent on standard orders,
where nothing is charged to you.

estimated_profit.description:
Your expected profit on this order — the same figure the Dropea dashboard shows you.

It is the order total minus the expenses you bear: the goods, fulfillment, shipping, the platform and COD commissions, and taxes. The tax figures follow the order's current state (delivered, refused or lost), so the value tracks what the order is actually settling at. Warranty orders use their own tax branch.

It is an estimate, not an invoiced amount: it moves with the order state until the order reaches a terminal one. Absent when the order has not been costed yet.

customer_reliability.description:
How reliably this customer has taken delivery in the past — the
same fingerprint the Dropea dashboard shows on the orders list.
Use it to spot buyers who habitually refuse deliveries before you
ship a cash-on-delivery order.

**Opt-in**: only returned when you pass `?include=reliability`.
It is left out by default because computing it aggregates the
phone's whole order history — cheap per page, but pointless
overhead for integrations that do not use it.

**Dropshipper only.** It describes the buyer, whose relationship
belongs to the dropshipper — the same reason the supplier surface
also withholds the buyer's contact details.

Keyed by the customer's phone number and computed across the
whole platform, not just your own orders. Absent when the order
carries no phone or the history could not be resolved.

level.description:
Bucket derived from `delivery_rate`: `GOOD` above 70%,
`MEDIUM` between 40% and 70%, `BAD` below 40%, and `UNKNOWN`
when the customer has no completed orders to judge by.

delivery_rate.description: delivered / (delivered + rejected). `null` when nothing is computable yet.

delivered_count.description: Orders this customer has taken delivery of.

tracking_number.description: Carrier tracking number of the order's latest shipment, derived from the order's tracking snapshot. Always present; `null` when the order has no tracking yet.

tracking_url.description: Public tracking URL for the order's latest shipment. Always present; `null` when the order has no tracking yet.

carrier.description:
Carrier code. The live list of valid codes is obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`).
Each entry includes its available `services[]`.

service_type.description:
Carrier-specific service code. The valid codes are obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`) —
inspect `services[].code` of the chosen carrier. Each carrier has
its own service codes. Examples: `EMS` (CTT), `24` (TIPSA), `74` (GLS).

external_order_id.description:
Optional external reference for the order, typically the order id
from the connected storefront (Shopify, WooCommerce, Tienda Nube,
etc.). Stored verbatim and echoed back on every order read so the
integrator can correlate Dropea orders with their source system.

UpdateOrderInput.description:
Partial-update payload for `PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}`. Every
field is optional; send only what changes.

`line_items`, when sent, **replaces the whole set of lines** of the
order: every line you want to keep must be in the list, packs
included. A pack line may carry `sub_order_line_items` to change what
the pack contains (see "Editing a pack" on the endpoint). Every
variant — lines and sub order line items — must belong to the same
supplier and share one fulfillment type.

line_items.description: The complete new set of lines of the order. Lines not listed are removed.

sub_order_line_items.description:
Only on a pack line (`variant_type: BUNDLE`). The FULL
composition of the pack, per pack unit.

- **Omitted** → the pack keeps the composition it currently
  has on this order (including any earlier edit).
- **Sent** → replaces the whole composition with exactly
  this set. To change one product of the pack, resend all
  of them.

Sending it on a line that is not a pack is rejected with
`PACK_COMPONENTS_NOT_A_PACK`. See "Editing a pack" on the
PATCH endpoint for every rule and error.

carrier.description:
Carrier code. The live list of valid codes is obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`).

service_type.description:
Carrier-specific service code. The valid codes are obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`) —
inspect `services[].code` of the chosen carrier.

UpdateCustomerDetails.description: Partial customer details. Every field is optional — send only what needs to change.

UpdateShippingAddress.description: Partial shipping address. Every field is optional. The joined street (`address_line_1` + `, ` + `address_line_2`) must not exceed 200 characters with destination MX and 100 elsewhere (`ADDRESS_LENGTH_EXCEEDED`).

field_extra_1.description: MX: colonia (neighbourhood), up to 60 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`. On edit, a field absent or `null` keeps the stored value; an empty string (`""`) clears it.

field_extra_2.description: MX: entre calles (cross streets), up to 100 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`. On edit, a field absent or `null` keeps the stored value; an empty string (`""`) clears it.

field_extra_3.description: MX: referencias (delivery references), up to 150 characters. Only stored when the destination country is MX (colonia / entre calles / referencias); outside MX they are ignored. Optional. Never truncated: a longer value is rejected with `ADDRESS_EXTRA_FIELD_TOO_LONG`. On edit, a field absent or `null` keeps the stored value; an empty string (`""`) clears it.

OrderOperationAsync.description: Async response body returned when a sync order mutation cannot complete within the saga timeout (15s). Clients should poll `/dropshipper/operations/{operation_id}` or `/supplier/operations/{operation_id}` to follow up.

message.example: saga did not complete within the configured timeout

ProductManufacturer.description:
Legal identification of the product maker (EU GPSR). Only the fields
the supplier filled in are present; omitted when none is.

image_id.description: Media id of the manufacturer logo.

eu_name.description: EU responsible person, when the maker is outside the EU.

variant_id.description: Human-readable sequential variant number. Same field name and value as the Supplier surface (`SupplierProductVariant.variant_id`) and as `OrderLineItemInput.variant_id` used to create orders.

recommended_sale_price.description:
**The price suggested to the end shopper (PVPR).** A commercial
reference set by the supplier — nobody is charged this amount by
Dropea. `0` means the supplier has not set a PVPR yet, not that
the variant is free.

Same field and meaning on the supplier surface
(`SupplierProductVariant.recommended_sale_price`).

Until I3121 this figure was published under `price`.

price.description:
**What you pay the supplier for this variant.** The price of the
actual transaction between you and them: the rate negotiated
with you when one exists, otherwise the supplier's general
wholesale price.

The supplier sees this same concept under the same name
(`SupplierProductVariant.price`), but from their side it is
always their general wholesale price — a rate negotiated with
one dropshipper is never disclosed to another party.

BREAKING CHANGE — `price` previously carried the PVPR, which now
lives in `recommended_sale_price`. A client reading `price` keeps
working but receives a different, lower figure: check any margin
or retail-price calculation built on it.

variant_type.description:
Variant type. Omitted when not set.
- `SIMPLE` — standard product variant (most common value).
- `DEFAULT` — a standard single variant (synonym of `SIMPLE`).
- `BUNDLE` — a pack: one line that ships several products together.

options.description: Variant options (e.g. color, size). Omitted when the variant has none.

weight.description: Variant weight in kg. Omitted when not set.

estimated_weight.description:
Estimated variant weight in kg, in the same unit as `weight`, derived
from the weights the carriers measured on shipped orders. `0` means
there is no estimate yet. Always present. Read-only: it is ignored
in request bodies and cannot be set through the API.

dimensions.description:
Box dimensions in centimetres. Omitted when the variant has none,
or when any of the three sides is missing.

ean.description: EAN/UPC code. Omitted when not set.

image_url.description:
Ready-to-use URL of this variant's image. `null` when the variant
has no image, or when the image could not be resolved at read time.

Product.description:
Product shape returned by the dropshipper-facing endpoints
(`/dropshipper/products`). Each variant carries two distinct prices:

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `price` | What **you pay** the supplier — the real transaction price |
| `recommended_sale_price` | The PVPR suggested to the end shopper |

The supplier's own internal cost (`cost_price` on their surface) is
never exposed here.

id.description: Human-readable sequential product number. Same value as `product_id`.

product_id.description: Human-readable sequential product number, under the name the supplier surface uses. Same value as `id`.

status.description:
Visibility status of the product on the public surface. Internal
lifecycle states (`PENDING_MODERATION`, `BLOCKED`, `INACTIVE`) are
filtered server-side and never surfaced — public consumers only
see purchasable products.
- `PUBLIC` — listed publicly, every variant available.
- `EXCLUSIVE` — only visible if the caller has an allocation on at least one variant.

owner_id.description: Human-readable sequential user number of the product owner (the supplier, or the dropshipper for its own packs). Same value as `owner_user_id`.

owner_user_id.description: Human-readable sequential user number of the product owner, under the name the supplier surface uses. Same value as `owner_id`.

media.description:
Media of the product as ready-to-use URLs — no id-to-URL lookup
needed on your side. Both arrays are always present and may be
empty. An asset that could not be resolved is omitted rather than
returned as an internal identifier.

fulfillment_price.description:
Fulfillment prices for this product, **scoped to your role**.
You receive the price **you are charged**; what the fulfiller is
paid is not part of your contract and is omitted.

Absent when the product carries no fulfillment pricing.

fulfillment_outbound_price.description: Price Dropea charges you to fulfil one order of this product.

fulfillment_refused_price.description: Same price when the order comes back refused.

extra_unit_price.description: Per-unit surcharge applied on top. Visible to every role.

extra_unit_refused_price.description: Same surcharge when the order comes back refused.

category_id.description:
Category of the product: the `category_id` of
`GET /dropshipper/products/categories`. `null` when the product
has a category without a public id; omitted when it has none.

is_featured.description: Whether Dropea features the product in the catalog.

is_favorite.description: Whether you marked the product as a favorite.

warranty_policy.description:
Warranty conditions that apply to the product: its own policy, or
the supplier's general policy when the product uses it. `null`
when there is none. **Only on the product detail endpoint**, never
on the listing (the text can be long).

store_type.description:
Storefront platform the shop is connected to.
- `SHOPIFY` / `WOOCOMMERCE` — managed integration with the platform.
- `GENERIC` — manually-created shop (no auto-sync).
- `UNKNOWN` — unclassified.

address_extra_fields_mapping.description:
Mapping between the order attributes written by the COD form of a
Shopify shop and the extra address fields of its orders
(`field_extra_1/2/3`, MX: colonia, entre calles, referencias).
It is configured in the Dropea app, only where the extra address
fields are enabled (MX). `null` when the shop is not SHOPIFY or
has no valid mapping. Always present in the full shop; never
returned with `?simple=true`.

sync_enabled.description:
Whether the synchronization between Dropea and the Shopify shop is
on (`PUT /dropshipper/shops/{id}/sync`). `null` when the shop is
not SHOPIFY. Always present in the full shop; never returned with
`?simple=true`.

provider.description: COD form whose order attributes feed the extra address fields.

field_extra_2.description: Attribute read into `field_extra_2` (MX entre calles). `null` = unmapped.

attribute_name.description: Name of the Shopify order attribute that feeds the field.

prefix.description: Fixed text the form puts before the value, removed when the order is imported. `null` = no prefix.

store_owner_id.description: Human-readable sequential user number of the store owner.

status.description: Top-level lifecycle status — same vocabulary as `Order.status`. See `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/order-statuses`. NOTE: `DELIVERED` top-level is **legacy** — the canonical terminal state is `FINISH` (with `sub_status: DELIVERED`); kept only for historical orders.

id.description: Auto-incremental numeric identifier assigned at incidence creation. Stable across the resource lifetime and used as the path parameter when transitioning state via `POST /(dropshipper|admin)/issues/{id}/resolve`.

order_id.description: Sequential numeric order identifier (`order_id`) of the order this incidence belongs to. Omitted when the incidence is not linked to an order.

owner_id.description: Sequential numeric dropshipper identifier (`user_id`) that owns the incidence.

type.description:
Normalized incidence type, derived server-side from the carrier-specific incidence code. The same vocabulary applies across CTT, GLS and TIPSA so integrators do not need carrier-specific dictionaries.

Possible values:
- `ADDRESS_INCORRECT` — the delivery address is wrong or incomplete and the carrier could not deliver.
- `RECIPIENT_ABSENT` — the recipient was not present during the delivery attempt.
- `REFUSED_BY_RECIPIENT` — the recipient refused the package.
- `DAMAGED_PACKAGE` — the package is damaged.
- `LOST_PACKAGE` — the package was declared lost by the carrier.
- `CUSTOMS_ISSUE` — held or stuck at customs.
- `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION` — the carrier needs additional authorization to proceed (e.g. recipient signature).
- `PENDING_DATA` — shipment data missing for the carrier to continue (e.g. phone, address complement).
- `POSSIBLE_RETURN` — the carrier anticipates a return to origin.
- `RETURN_REQUESTED` — return to origin was requested.
- `RETAINED` — package retained somewhere in the carrier network (not customs-related).
- `ADMINISTRATIVE_ISSUE` — carrier-internal administrative issue.
- `DELIVERY_FAILED` — delivery attempt failed without a specific cause.
- `GENERAL_INCIDENCE` — generic incidence when the carrier code does not map to any category above.

status.description:
User workflow over the incidence. Independent of the package operational state (`is_active`).

Allowed transitions: `PENDING -> {MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT, RESOLVED}` and `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT -> RESOLVED`. INFO never transitions; RESOLVED is final.

Possible values:
- `INFO` — informational; the carrier reported an event that does not require DP action (the carrier resolution matrix offers no options).
- `PENDING` — just created, requires DP action.
- `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` — the DP already contacted the customer and still owes the carrier a solution. NOT a final state: the issue stays pending to resolve and accepts a transition to `RESOLVED`.
- `RESOLVED` — a concrete resolution was applied. The resolution type lives in `resolution_status` and its payload in `resolution_data`. Final state.

resolution_status.description:
Concrete resolution applied by the DP when `status == RESOLVED`. `null` for INFO/PENDING/MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT.

Each value pairs with a specific `resolution_data` shape:
- `RETRY` — `resolution_data = { date, time_window }`. Retry the delivery.
- `CHANGE_ADDRESS` — `resolution_data = { address: {...} }`. Redirect the package.
- `PICKUP_AT_AGENCY` — `resolution_data = null`. The recipient collects from the carrier agency.
- `RETURN_REQUESTED` — `resolution_data = null`. Return the package to origin.
- `SOLUTION_PROVIDED` — `resolution_data = null`. Free-text solution (aportar solución, TIPSA / GLS ES). The text is supplied on the resolve request as `resolution_note` and is NOT echoed back on the resource.

initial_carrier_substatus_code.description: Carrier-specific sub-status code that opened the incidence. CTT stores `reason` or `reason/situation` (e.g. `"11/B"`). TIPSA stores the carrier's incidence code (e.g. `"NAM"`, `"DO"`), except `"DO_AUTO"`: a value of ours, not TIPSA's, for the automatic 7-day return notice (a `DO` with no agency observation), which is informational. GLS ES stores its incidence `codificado`. `null` for carriers that report no sub-status.

distance_km.description: Delivery distance in kilometres of the carrier's destination agency, captured when the incidence was opened. TIPSA-only; `null` for every other carrier and for TIPSA incidences whose creation could not read it. `0` is a legitimate value, not a placeholder for unknown.

absence_count.description: Number of distinct days the carrier reported a failed delivery attempt (recipient absent) for this tracking number. Counted from the carrier's own event list, not from the number of issue records. `null` means unknown — issues created before this field existed, and carriers whose polling never exposes a raw event timeline. `0` is a real reading.

is_first_absent.description: `true` when this is the recipient's FIRST failed delivery attempt on this tracking number (`type` is `RECIPIENT_ABSENT` and `absence_count` is 1). A first absence is usually self-resolving, since the carrier normally retries the next day. `false` for a repeat absence or any other issue type. `null` when `absence_count` is unknown, so "not the first" stays distinguishable from "unknown".

allowed_resolution_options.description: Resolution options the carrier accepts for this incidence in its current state. Computed by shipping-service from `(carrier, carrier_status_code, carrier_substatus_code)`. Empty array when the carrier does not support resolution.

is_active.description:
Operational state — `true` while the carrier still reports incidence for this tracking; `false` once it was closed.

- **Automatic closure**: shipping-service flips it to `false` as soon as the package leaves `INCIDENCE` (e.g. EMG/EMI webhook after an EMH) and sets `resolved_at`. It does NOT touch `status`, `resolution_status` or `resolution_data` — the user workflow is preserved.
- **Manual change via API**: `POST /(dropshipper|admin)/issues/{id}/resolve` ONLY changes `status`, `resolution_status`, `resolution_data` (and stamps `resolution_changed_at`). It does NOT touch `is_active` or `resolved_at`.

To list what needs attention: `is_active=true`. For history closed by the carrier: `is_active=false`.

resolution_data.description: Additional payload persisted when `status == RESOLVED` and `resolution_status` is `RETRY` or `CHANGE_ADDRESS`. `null` for every other case (including PICKUP_AT_AGENCY and RETURN_REQUESTED).

resolution_changed_at.description:
Timestamp of the last `status` change made by the dropshipper / admin via API (`POST /(dropshipper|admin)/issues/{id}/resolve`). Independent of `resolved_at` (carrier closure).

- `null` while the incidence stays in `INFO` or `PENDING`.
- Set once when the incidence transitions out of `PENDING` (transitions are one-shot).

resolved_at.description: Timestamp of the automatic carrier-side closure (when `is_active` flips to `false` because of DELIVERED / OUT_FOR_DELIVERY). Manual API changes do NOT populate this field — use `resolution_changed_at` for that.

pickup_point.description: Pickup point associated with the incidence (carrier-side store / agency / locker where the package is available). Only populated when the carrier reported a pickup event that identifies the point (CTT `EMW`) and the point was synced to the catalog. In every other case (most incidences) it is `null` — the key is always present.

PickupPointDayHours.description:
Opening hours for a single day at a pickup point. The carrier
exposes up to two windows per day (morning / afternoon). Closed
windows come through as `null`.

day.description: Day of the week in lowercase (`monday`..`sunday`).

PickupPoint.description:
Pickup point (carrier-agnostic) where the recipient can collect
the package. shipping-service resolves it from the identifier
the carrier reports in the event and exposes all its fields.
Fields not provided by the carrier come through as `null`;
`hours` may be an empty array.

pup_id.description: Carrier-side identifier of the pickup point.

is_active.description: Whether the pickup point is currently operational.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last sync from the carrier catalog.

ResolutionRetry.description:
`resolution_data` payload accepted (and persisted) when
`resolution_status == RETRY`. Captures the new delivery attempt
the DP wants the carrier to make.

date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the retry should be attempted.

ResolutionAddress.description:
Address sub-document for the CHANGE_ADDRESS resolution. Mirrors the
order's `shipping_address` shape: free-text `street` (including the
house number), optional `address_line_2`, plus `postal_code`,
`city`, `state` (province / region), and ISO-2 `country`.

`zone`, `cross_streets` and `reference` are the extra address
components Mexican addressing uses. They are optional in this schema
because no other carrier accepts them, but they are REQUIRED when the
issue belongs to a QualityPost (MX) shipment: QualityPost will not apply
the correction without them, and a resolution submitted without them is
rejected. `postal_code` is immutable on QualityPost's side — send the one
already on the shipment; a changed value makes the correction fail rather
than silently diverge.

zone.description: Neighbourhood (Mexican colonia). Required for QualityPost (MX) issues.

cross_streets.description: Streets the address sits between. Required for QualityPost (MX) issues.

reference.description: Visual reference of the address. Required for QualityPost (MX) issues.
reference.example: Porton negro, frente a la farmacia

ResolutionChangeAddress.description:
`resolution_data` payload accepted (and persisted) when
`resolution_status == CHANGE_ADDRESS`. Wraps the new address the
carrier must redirect the parcel to.

ResolveIssueInput.description:
Payload accepted by `POST /(dropshipper|admin)/issues/{id}/resolve`.

Transitions a `PENDING` or `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` issue to one of the
two user-driven states (`MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` or `RESOLVED`). Only
`RESOLVED` is final: an issue already in `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` can
still be resolved (it just records that the client was contacted).

Combinations:
  - `status=MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT`: `resolution_status` and
    `resolution_data` MUST be absent.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=RETRY`:
    `resolution_data = { date, time_window }` REQUIRED.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=CHANGE_ADDRESS`:
    `resolution_data = { address: {...} }` REQUIRED.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=PICKUP_AT_AGENCY`:
    `resolution_data` MUST be absent.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=RETURN_REQUESTED`:
    `resolution_data` MUST be absent.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=SOLUTION_PROVIDED`:
    `resolution_data` MUST be absent and `resolution_note` is REQUIRED
    (free-text solution — TIPSA / GLS ES "aportar solución").

`resolution_note` is a free-text note (max 500 chars). Optional in
general, but REQUIRED when `resolution_status = SOLUTION_PROVIDED`.
Forwarded to the carrier when it supports a resolution push (e.g.
TIPSA). It is REQUEST-ONLY: it never appears on the Issue resource
(`GET /dropshipper/issues/{id}`) nor in the `issue.resolved` webhook.

The 500-char limit is the limit of the FIELD, which is stored and
shown in full. What reaches the CARRIER can be shorter: TIPSA accepts
at most 100 characters per action and truncates silently, so for a
TIPSA shipment only the first ~100 characters of the note are
registered with the carrier — cut on a word boundary, after the
structured instruction. Each carrier caps it differently — GLS ES
records at most 80 — while what is stored and returned stays complete.

resolution_data.description:
Required iff `resolution_status` is `RETRY` (with
`date` + `time_window`) or `CHANGE_ADDRESS` (with `address`).
Forbidden otherwise.

resolution_note.description:
Optional free-text note (max 500 chars) forwarded to the carrier
for carriers that support a resolution push (TIPSA, GLS ES,
QualityPost). It IS persisted on the incidence, but it is never
returned on the Issue resource or the `issue.resolved` webhook —
same precedent as `carrier_acknowledged_at`.
resolution_note.example: Cliente confirmó nueva dirección por teléfono.

id.description: Sequential `store_id` of the shop. Use this value as the `{id}` path param on `/dropshipper/shops/{id}` and related endpoints.

OperationStatus.description:
Polling response returned by `/supplier/operations/{id}` and
`/dropshipper/operations/{id}`. Reflects the cached state of the saga that
the original mutation kicked off, so clients can recover from a
504 saga-wait timeout without re-issuing the request (which would
risk a duplicate side-effect on the server).

operation_id.description: The same value as the `Idempotency-Key` you sent on the original mutation, echoed back in its 504 body — poll with the key you already have.

status.description:
- `in_progress`: the saga is still running.
- `completed`: the saga finished with a 2xx response. `result` is set.
- `failed`: the saga finished with a 4xx response. `error` is set.

result.description: Response payload of the original mutation. Only set when `status == completed`.

error.description: Failure details of the original mutation. Only set when `status == failed`.

resource.description: Best-effort pointer to the affected resource derived from the response body.

PvProductCategory.description:
Read-only product category projection returned by
`GET /supplier/products/categories`. Identified by `category_id`,
a public auto-incremental integer handle. Suppliers pass this number
back via `category_id` in product create / update payloads.

parent_id.description: Parent category number when categories are nested. Omitted at the top of the tree.

Webhook.description: Webhook subscription attached to an API Key.

topic.description:
Canonical topic the subscription is bound to. One of the
stable snake-case values listed in the Webhooks tag overview.

url.description: Destination URL where webhook payloads are POSTed.

active.description:
Whether the subscription is active. Auto-deactivated after 3
consecutive failed deliveries; re-enable from the API Keys
section of your Dropea dashboard.

topic.description:
Topic the subscription binds to. One of the dropshipper webhook
topics listed in the Webhooks tag overview. An unknown topic is
rejected with `400`.

ShopProductLinkInput.description:
Body for `POST /dropshipper/shops/{id}/products/link`. The

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Subscribe one or more webhook URLs per API Key from the **API Keys** section of your Dropea dashboard to receive real-time POSTs when Dropea resources change. Each API Key holds an independent list of `(topic, URL)` pairs. ### Public topics - **`order.created`** — New order created. `resource` is modeled identically to the GET order response. A pack is one line with `variant_type: BUNDLE`; on a dropshipper subscription it carries `sub_order_line_items` (products and units per pack, as in `GET /dropshipper/orders/{id}`), omitted on old orders without a frozen composition. - **`order.status.changed`** — Order state machine transitioned, or the order was edited (lines, address, payment method, carrier or the composition of a pack — the status may then be unchanged). The current state lives in `resource.status` / `resource.sub_status`. Integrators that need to detect specific transitions should cache the last seen state per `resource_id`. On a dropshipper subscription a pack line carries its current `sub_order_line_items`, including an edit made with `PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}`; a provider subscription receives packs expanded into component rows, without `sub_order_line_items`. - **`order.cancelled`** — Order cancelled (by dropshipper, supplier or system). - **`issue.created`** — A new shipment incidence was created. **Branch on `resource.status` + `resource.is_active`**: action is required only when `status="PENDING" && is_active=true`. - **`issue.status.changed`** — The dropshipper updated the workflow status of an incidence. `resource.is_active` reflects whether the carrier still has it open. - **`issue.resolved`** — A shipment incidence was closed — typically because the carrier moved the shipment out of INCIDENCE. Each topic's payload schema is documented under **Sample payloads by topic** below, with the schema name pointing to the **Models** sidebar section for the full field reference. ### Headers sent with every delivery - `X-Dropea-Topic` — topic name (matches `topic` in the body). - `X-Dropea-Event-Id` — UUID per delivery. Store it for idempotent processing. - `X-Dropea-Signature` — `sha256=`. Verify with a constant-time comparison over the raw request body bytes (see **Verifying signatures** below). The `signing_secret` is shown ONCE when you create the API Key — it is shared by all webhook subscriptions (topics) created under that key, not regenerated per subscription — store it server-side. ### Verifying signatures Always verify the signature before processing the body — anyone who knows your URL could otherwise forge a request. ``` signature = "sha256=" + base64( HMAC_SHA256(raw_request_body, signing_secret) ) ``` - **The signing secret is the HMAC key, used as-is.** It is a 64-character hexadecimal string. Pass that exact string to your HMAC function as the key (its UTF-8 bytes). Do **not** decode it from hex or Base64 first: a decoded secret is a different key and the signature will never match. - **Sign the raw request body** — the exact bytes you received, before any JSON parsing. Re-serializing a parsed object (key order, spacing, number formatting) changes the bytes and breaks the signature. - **Nothing else is signed**: there is no timestamp and no header in the signed string, only the body. - The digest is **Base64** (not hex), prefixed with `sha256=`. - Compare with a **constant-time** function — `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (Node.js), `hmac.compare_digest` (Python), `hash_equals` (PHP) — never with `==` / `===`. **Test vector** — check your code offline with these exact values: ``` signing_secret = 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08 raw_body = {"topic":"order.cancelled","event_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"} X-Dropea-Signature = sha256=IKoJQrqiOmdXLf9FwEIiRn3K/nFs7OD21DIPcPkx9fs= ``` If you get `sha256=whoW4EfHb0bKGH+CAah9ia5q/Xf1bQ97YLgCjVO3uPg=` instead, you decoded the secret from hex.
Node.js (Express) ```js const crypto = require('crypto'); const express = require('express'); const app = express(); const SIGNING_SECRET = process.env.DROPEA_SIGNING_SECRET; // the 64-char string, as-is app.post('/webhooks/dropea', express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }), (req, res) => { const received = req.header('X-Dropea-Signature') || ''; const expected = 'sha256=' + crypto .createHmac('sha256', SIGNING_SECRET) .update(req.body) // raw Buffer, not a re-serialized object .digest('base64'); const ok = received.length === expected.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(received), Buffer.from(expected)); if (!ok) return res.status(401).end(); const event = JSON.parse(req.body.toString('utf8')); res.status(200).end(); }); ```
Python (Flask) ```python import base64, hashlib, hmac, os from flask import Flask, request app = Flask(__name__) SIGNING_SECRET = os.environ["DROPEA_SIGNING_SECRET"].encode() # as-is, NOT bytes.fromhex() @app.post("/webhooks/dropea") def handle(): raw = request.get_data() # raw bytes, before any JSON parsing expected = "sha256=" + base64.b64encode( hmac.new(SIGNING_SECRET, raw, hashlib.sha256).digest() ).decode() received = request.headers.get("X-Dropea-Signature", "") if not hmac.compare_digest(received, expected): return "", 401 event = request.get_json() return "", 200 ```
PHP ```php ### Body structure (v2 envelope) Every webhook uses the same flat envelope. Resource state lives inside `resource`, modeled byte-for-byte after the public REST representation for the same resource (e.g. `GET /dropshipper/orders/{order_number}` for order webhooks, `GET /supplier/products/{product_id}` for product webhooks). A GET of the same resource returns the same shape. - `topic` — string. Matches the `X-Dropea-Topic` header. - `market` — string. Market of the deploy that emitted the event (e.g. `"PT"`, `"ES"`, `"IT"`) — varies per deploy/market. - `event_id` — string. UUID v4, identical to `X-Dropea-Event-Id`. Use it for idempotent processing. - `event_at` — string. UTC timestamp of the event itself, ISO 8601 (`2026-05-21T14:32:11.000Z`). - `resource_id` — integer. Sequential numeric id of the resource (matches `resource.id` / `resource.product_id` / etc). - `resource` — object. Snapshot of the resource at emission time. **Status values are uppercase** (`PENDING`, `CONFIRMED.PENDING_SUPPLIER`, `FINISH.CANCELLED`, `PUBLIC`, `INACTIVE`, ...) — same enums the REST endpoints return. > The envelope does NOT carry a `previous_state` field. Integrators that need to detect specific transitions (`PROCESSING.PICKING → PROCESSING.PACKED`, etc.) should cache the last seen `resource.status` / `resource.sub_status` keyed by `resource_id` and diff on each delivery — same pattern used by Shopify and GitHub. Body keys are emitted in this order so the payload reads as a narrative: **what + where → delivery identity (id + when) → resource snapshot**. ### Sample payloads by topic Click any topic to expand its sample payload.
order.created **Schema:** `WebhookOrderCreated` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "order.created", "market": "PT", "event_id": "24cdc4a3-7e0f-4d7b-bb5a-3c2af7c5b87c", "event_at": "2026-05-21T14:32:11.000Z", "resource_id": 14, "resource": { /* full Order shape — same as GET /dropshipper/orders/14 */ } } ```
order.status.changed **Schema:** `WebhookOrderStatusChanged` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "order.status.changed", "market": "PT", "event_id": "0d1f7d4a-9216-4f9c-9c8b-bc1d8b9f5d2e", "event_at": "2026-05-21T14:32:11.000Z", "resource_id": 14, "resource": { /* full Order shape */ } } ```
order.cancelled **Schema:** `WebhookOrderCancelled` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "order.cancelled", "market": "PT", "event_id": "2b4a9c8d-3e5f-4a1b-8c2d-7e9f1a3b5c7d", "event_at": "2026-05-21T15:11:42.000Z", "resource_id": 14, "resource": { /* full Order shape — status = FINISH, sub_status = CANCELLED */ } } ```
issue.created **Schema:** `WebhookIssueCreated` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "issue.created", "market": "PT", "event_id": "3a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d", "event_at": "2026-05-21T10:15:00.000Z", "resource_id": 5, "resource": { /* full Issue shape — same as the list endpoint item */ } } ```
issue.status.changed **Schema:** `WebhookIssueStatusChanged` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "issue.status.changed", "market": "PT", "event_id": "9f8e7d6c-5b4a-3928-bcde-1f2e3d4c5b6a", "event_at": "2026-05-21T11:00:00.000Z", "resource_id": 5, "resource": { /* full Issue shape */ } } ```
issue.resolved **Schema:** `WebhookIssueResolved` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "issue.resolved", "market": "PT", "event_id": "7e6d5c4b-3a29-4f1e-8d7c-6b5a4938271f", "event_at": "2026-05-21T15:00:00.000Z", "resource_id": 5, "resource": { /* full Issue shape — status = RESOLVED */ } } ```
### Delivery contract Reply with any `2xx` within **5 seconds**. Failures are retried with a constant `1m / 5m / 15m` backoff. After 3 consecutive failed attempts the subscription is auto-deactivated — you must re-enable it from the **API Keys** section of your Dropea dashboard.

post.description:
Move a `PENDING` or `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` issue to one of the two
user-driven states. Only owned issues can be transitioned — the API
Key owner is the only one allowed to mutate them. INFO issues are
immutable here and RESOLVED is final; `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` is not,
so an issue already being managed with the client can still be
resolved.

Body shape (validated by the route):

  - `status` (required) — `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` or `RESOLVED`.
  - `resolution_status` (required iff `status=RESOLVED`) — one of
    `RETRY`, `CHANGE_ADDRESS`, `PICKUP_AT_AGENCY`, `RETURN_REQUESTED`.
  - `resolution_data` (required iff `resolution_status` is `RETRY`
    or `CHANGE_ADDRESS`) — `{date, time_window}` or `{address}`.

The successful response stamps `resolution_changed_at` with the
current timestamp.

A rejection coming from the shipping layer is answered with its own
status and a stable `failure.code`, so it can be branched on instead
of retried. These rejections are permanent for the request as sent —
retrying it unchanged yields the same answer:

  - `INCIDENCE_CLOSED` (400) — the issue is already closed.
  - `INVALID_INCIDENCE_TRANSITION` (400) — the current status cannot
    reach the requested one.
  - `RESOLUTION_STATUS_REQUIRED` / `RESOLUTION_STATUS_NOT_ALLOWED` (400).
  - `RESOLUTION_DATA_REQUIRED` / `RESOLUTION_DATA_NOT_ALLOWED` (400).
  - `RESOLUTION_NOTE_REQUIRED` / `INVALID_RESOLUTION_OPTION` (400).
  - `NOT_LATEST_INCIDENCE` (409) — a newer incidence supersedes this one.

A `503` means the shipping layer was unreachable and the request was
not applied — that one is safe to retry.

post.description:
Creates an order **synchronously**. The endpoint publishes the
saga-initiating event on NATS and waits up to 15s for it to settle:

- **200** — the saga completed in time; the response body is the
  full created order.
- **504** — the saga did not settle within the timeout. The body
  carries an `operation_id` you can poll via
  `GET /dropshipper/operations/{operation_id}`. This
  `operation_id` is **the same value as the `Idempotency-Key`
  you sent**, so you poll with the key you already have. On a
  late success the `order.created` webhook
  also fires; if creation fails there is no dedicated webhook —
  poll the operation above instead.

Validation of the requested store and line items happens inline
before the event is published — an unknown `store_id` or line
items that span multiple suppliers surface as 400. Order-service
additionally enforces that the authenticated caller owns the
target store (see 403 below); admin-scoped keys and Shopify
webhook orders are exempt.

This endpoint requires a unique `Idempotency-Key` header — replayed
requests with the same key return the cached response.

200.description: Saga completed within timeout; returns the created order.

403.description:
Forbidden. Three scenarios return 403: the API key is missing the
`orders:create` permission, the authenticated caller does
not own the target store (the create is rejected with
`CREATOR_NOT_STORE_OWNER` before the saga runs), OR the supplier
of the items may not sell in this market — either no signed
platform contract (`SUPPLIER_CONTRACT_NOT_SIGNED`) or a fiscal
standing that no longer allows it
(`SUPPLIER_TAX_DATA_GRACE_EXPIRED`,
`SUPPLIER_TAX_DATA_RESIGN_PENDING`).

504.description: Saga did not complete within 15s. Client should poll the operation id.

get.description:
Fetch a single order visible to the authenticated owner.

**Packs.** A pack is ONE line with `variant_type: BUNDLE`. Its content is listed in
that line's `sub_order_line_items`: one entry per product, with `quantity` = units
of that product in ONE pack. Units shipped = line `quantity` × sub line `quantity` (in the
example, 3 packs × 2 t-shirts = 6 t-shirts). It is the composition frozen on this
order — the catalog one at the time of sale, or the one you set with
`PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}` (see "Editing a pack" there) — and it may be
missing on old orders placed before the composition was frozen on the order.
The line carries no internal ids or supplier prices of its sub order line items.

parameters.description: Sequential order number (order_number).

Opt into extra, more expensive fields. Pass `reliability` to add
`customer_reliability` (the customer fingerprint) to each order —
